preconditions.expression: all(0 <= h(si, sj) <= 105 for si in [s1, s2, s3, s4] for sj in [s1, s2, s3, s4] if si != sj)
preconditions.description: All Hamming distances are non-negative and do not exceed 105.

preconditions.expression: any(h(si, sj) > 0 for si in [s1, s2, s3, s4] for sj in [s1, s2, s3, s4] if si != sj)
preconditions.description: At least one Hamming distance is positive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s1) == len(s2) == len(s3) == len(s4) for s1, s2, s3, s4 in [[s1, s2, s3, s4]])
preconditions.description: All strings have the same length.

postconditions.expression: output == -1 or (output['len'] is not None and output['len'] > 0 and all(len(s) == output['len'] for s in output['strings']))
postconditions.description: If output is -1, there is no suitable set of strings. Otherwise, the output contains the length of each string and all strings are of that length.

postconditions.expression: output == -1 or all(h(s1, s2) == h(output['strings'][s1_idx], output['strings'][s2_idx]) for s1 in range(4) for s2 in range(s1 + 1, 4))
postconditions.description: If output is not -1, the pairwise Hamming distances between the restored strings are the same as between John's strings.

postconditions.expression: output == -1 or min(len(s) for s in output['strings']) == output['len']
postconditions.description: The output contains the set of strings with the minimum length.
